articles.title: Lutnick agrees to testify before Congress as Republicans pile on the embattled Commerce secretary
articles.summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has reportedly agreed to testify before lawmakers next month as the spotlight on him grows harsher amid Nvidia's turmoil.
articles.body:
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has reportedly agreed to testify before lawmakers next month as the spotlight on him grows harsher amid Nvidia's ( NVDA ) turmoil.

Both Democrats and Republicans alike are raising questions about whether Lutnick went too far in protecting Nvidia's push to sell its chips overseas even as the US government was warning about a possible security breach.

Lutnick is reportedly set to appear on Dec. 10 before the Senate Banking Committee, in news first reported by Fox News. Spokespersons for the Commerce Department and the Senate panel did not immediately provide additional details.

The appearance would set up what could be a major moment for the suddenly embattled Commerce secretary after days in which he and the White House had largely stayed silent as even some of Trump's closest allies grew more vocal.

Lutnick will appear before Republican Sen. Tim Scott of South Carolina, the chairman of the Senate panel until the end of the year and a regular on President Trump's campaign stops last month. Scott released a letter Thursday evening requesting that Lutnick and ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang appear before Congress early next month.

"Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive U.S. technology," Scott wrote. "The American people deserve answers."

Republican Sen. John Kennedy of Louisiana used more colorful language in a recent appearance on CNN , saying he wanted answers about why the Commerce Department allowed Nvidia to sell chips to an alleged Chinese spy's company.

"This whole thing is an intergalactic freak show," Kennedy said.

Some Trump aides have declined to defend Lutnick emphatically.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent raised eyebrows Friday during a CNBC appearance when he reiterated his desire for stronger government limits on advanced semiconductor exports — which he added that the Pentagon, State Department, and the trade representative's office agreed with.

"Commerce has the pen…," Bessent said, "and you will have to ask them about their internal processes."

Nvidia CEO Huang resigns amid affair scandals

Who is Colette Kress, Nvidia's new interim CEO?

3 challenges for a post-Jensen Huang Nvidia

The rapid-fire developments have also increased the odds of Congress passing new curbs on semiconductor exports to China, with lawmakers now moving to add some combination of three bipartisan plans into a military funding bill that needs to pass before the end of the year.

A White House official said that Trump maintains confidence in Lutnick, but the president's only direct reaction to the scandal in recent days was a Truth Social post saying Huang had "done a fantastic job" and that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over Nvidia.

articles.title: From the jungles of Bastar to the cells of Tihar Jail: Aruna Lohia Goenka on the power of Hunar
articles.summary: Drawing upon almost 3 decades of work in national development, Impact Catalyst Aruna Lohia Goenka developed YASHA, her five-pillar framework for Viksit
articles.body: Drawing upon almost 3 decades of work in national development, Impact Catalyst Aruna Lohia Goenka developed YASHA, her five-pillar framework for Viksit Bharat 2047. In this edition of the Knowledge Series, Sanjiv Kaura, CEO-CSR, The Times of India, speaks with Aruna Lohia Goenka about Hunar - the power of skills to transform lives.Sanjiv Kaura: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 2026 Diwali visit to Bastar in Chhattisgarh must have stirred some memories. Wasn't that where your journey into skilling began, under rather unusual circumstances?Aruna Lohia Goenka: Indeed, Sanjiv! The Bastar of the 1990s was very different from the Bastar we see today. It was a region deeply affected by Maoist violence, where opportunities for tribal communities were severely limited. We began opening schools and introducing what we then called vocational services - today's more fashionable term being skilling!And do you know what struck me, Sanjiv? I seem to have inherited a rather unusual family addiction! My father had an addiction to opening schools, sometimes so quietly and anonymously that we discovered some of them only after his passing. My brothers, meanwhile, seem to have developed an addiction to creating employment opportunities wherever they go!The industrial enterprise my father and brothers built now has a presence in some 40 countries, principally in manufacturing and materials. But the family's interests occasionally take rather unexpected turns - organic farming in Tuscany, cotton cultivation in Uzbekistan! Different geographies, different pursuits, but one common thread: generating employment is in our DNA!And there is another connection I find rather charming. My father and my brother established schools in the jungles of Indonesia back in the 1970s. Decades later, there I was, opening schools and working with tribal communities in Bastar and other parts of India!Closer home, our family also established a women's college and polytechnic in Kurukshetra, Haryana. And here's something that gives me particular satisfaction: three of its alumnae have gone on to join the IAS! Imagine that - from a classroom in Kurukshetra to the corridors of national administration!(Laughs) I suppose addictions run in families. Fortunately, ours seem to be socially productive!Perhaps that is the thread connecting it all. Whether it is an industrial enterprise, a farm in Tuscany or a school deep in the forests of Bastar, the setting changes, but the underlying aspiration remains remarkably similar - to create opportunities for people to learn, work and build lives of dignity.And seeing Bastar's transformation today gives me enormous satisfaction.When you open a school in a place like Bastar, you are not merely opening a school. You are opening a future.Sanjiv Kaura: Bastar was challenging enough. But surely you didn't stop there?Aruna Lohia Goenka: (Laughs) Apparently, I have a weakness for difficult-to-reach places!From the forests of Bastar, my journey took me to the mountains of Himachal Pradesh, particularly Chamba, historically one of India's more backward districts and now part of NITI Aayog’s Aspirational Districts Programme. We established 50 skilling centres across Chamba district, bringing opportunities closer to communities that had long been underserved.You see, Sanjiv, talent is remarkably democratic. Opportunity, unfortunately, is not! A child's postal address should never determine the limits of their future.That is where Hunar becomes such a powerful equaliser.Sanjiv Kaura: From remote villages to the corridors of power! How did you end up training the Delhi Police?Aruna Lohia Goenka: That was an unexpected invitation! Former Delhi Police Commissioner B. K. Gupta asked whether we could help strengthen spoken English and soft skills within the police force. We mobilised resources through Teach India and began training Delhi Police personnel. I remain grateful to Commissioner B. K. Gupta for placing his trust in us. He was so pleased with the initiative that he extended an invitation to work in Tihar Jail, where he had earlier served as its chief before becoming Delhi Police Commissioner. There, we could help inmates, particularly those approaching release, acquire the skills and confidence to prepare for life beyond prison walls.Sanjiv Kaura: And then, somehow, you landed in Tihar Jail! Should I be concerned!?!Aruna Lohia Goenka: (Laughs) You are not the first to ask! There were occasions when friends would call my home and be told, quite casually, "She's gone to Tihar Jail." The silence at the other end was sometimes rather long! I suspect a few were already contemplating whether to arrange a lawyer!But jokes apart, Tihar remains one of the most satisfying places in which I have worked. Many inmates approaching release face an enormous challenge. Society may have served them a sentence, but it is often reluctant to offer them a second chance. Through skilling, communication and confidence-building, we prepared them for that second chance. A prison sentence may take away someone's freedom for a time. It should never take away their hope.And Sanjiv, sometimes the most important skill we can teach someone is the confidence to begin again.Sanjiv Kaura: (Laughs) Fortunately, Tihar wasn't your only classroom in Delhi! What else were you experimenting with?Aruna Lohia Goenka: Ashok Kumar Nigam, the then Commissioner of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), heard about our skilling initiatives and, inspired by the work we were already doing in other parts of Delhi, generously gave us access to, and space within, MCD schools, including those in the Defence Colony area, to introduce vocational skills such as beauty services and stitching. I remember how important it was to give young people skills they could actually use. Acquiring a skill gives a person immense confidence, a sense of self-worth and dignity. In other words, the ability to create one's own universe!And Sanjiv, never underestimate a skill simply because it does not come with a fancy designation!Sanjiv Kaura: Your views about India's demographic dividend?Aruna Lohia Goenka: Absolutely, Sanjiv! A demographic dividend is an opportunity, not an entitlement! Millions of young people are an enormous advantage - provided they have the skills, else our demographic dividend risks becoming a demographic bulge. That is why, in employability programmes such as Teach India, with which I am associated, we set a high bar: a minimum of 65% of our learners must secure gainful employment after completing their skilling programme. We measure success by livelihoods, not merely certificates!And remember, a skill should open a door, not become a ceiling.Sanjiv Kaura: Finally, how does Hunar fit into your vision of Viksit Bharat 2047?Aruna Lohia Goenka: Sanjiv, for me, Hunar is the bridge between human potential and human dignity. Be it tribal communities in Bastar, or youth in the Chamba hills, or students in government schools or personnel in Delhi police, or inmates in Tihar Jail, I see one common aspiration: People want to learn. They want to earn. They want to contribute. And above all, they want to live with dignity.We often say India has 1.4 billion people. I see 1.4 billion possibilities! Our task is to turn those possibilities into capabilities, those capabilities into livelihoods, and those livelihoods into a more prosperous, inclusive and confident Bharat.That is the Hunar I believe in. And that is the India I dream of!Disclaimer: This article has been produced on behalf of Aruna Goenka for Times Foundation as part of the Knowledge Sharing Series and published by Times Internet's Spotlight team.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: What the Nvidia scandal means for the company's earnings next week
articles.summary: Nvidia's earnings come a week after now-former CEO Jensen Huang's affair scandals rocked the company and tech world.
articles.body:
The fallout from the Nvidia ( NVDA ) board's ousting of co-founder Jensen Huang from his long-held role as CEO continues to reverberate across the tech and business worlds.

CFO Colette Kress has taken the reins as interim CEO , but myriad questions remain, ranging from who will become the next permanent leader of one of the world's most consequential companies to whether it will perform as well as before Huang's affair scandals broke.

All of this comes as Nvidia is scheduled to report its third quarter earnings next Tuesday.

This past week's upheaval won't impact earnings this quarter or next. Nvidia has sales locked in well in advance, meaning its bottom line won't take a hit for some time, if at all.

Nvidia is expected to report earnings per share (EPS) of $2.47 on revenue of $109.2 billion. That's a 90% increase in EPS and a 91% jump in revenue versus the same period last year.

Kress will have to acknowledge Huang's departure and the company's plans moving forward during the call. And analysts will have plenty of questions.

A number of analysts have already either downgraded or cut their price targets on Nvidia stock.

Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon, who reduced his price target from $400 to $200 and lowered his rating from Outperform to Market Perform, wrote in an investor note that Kress's appointment is a positive for the company.

"We see considerable uncertainty around further newsflow that is probably going to be coming down the pipe, as well as the ability of any new CEO to truly fill Jensen's shoes given how tightly he managed the direction of the business and its relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, and the broader industry ecosystem," Rasgon wrote in a note to investors.

Baird Equity Research analyst Tristan Gerra said Huang's resignation turns a page for Nvidia but that the episode hasn't hit its bottom yet.

"Headwinds include potential incremental senior management departures, H200 write-down charges, potential risk channel revenue adjustments, potential litigation [and] fines, uncertainties until [a] new CEO is announced along with the risk of some market share loss in 2029 as customers make contingency plans on a major top management transition and looking beyond the current product roadmap, along with more clarity on the next CEO's views regarding customer financings," Gerra wrote in an investor note Thursday.

articles.title: Nvidia director sold nearly $1B in stock weeks before the Jensen Huang scandal broke — and no trading plan was flagged
articles.summary: Huang stepped down as CEO after reports of a second extramarital relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell emerged.
articles.body:
Nvidia's second-largest shareholder sold about $946 million in company stock in the months leading up to CEO Jensen Huang's resignation on Nov. 12.

Nvidia [NASDAQ: NVDA] Board Director Mark Stevens was one of the top AI sellers in Q3 2026, selling roughly 4.2 million shares , according to filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. There were three separate batches of stock sales from Stevens, who joined the Nvidia board in 2008 following an earlier stint as a director from 1993 to 2006.

Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

The first common stock sale took place from Aug. 31 to Sept. 2 at equity prices ranging from $220 to $226, generating $411 million in new cash. The second sale stretched from Sept. 3 to Sept. 4 at prices ranging between $227 to $234 per share, garnering about $236 million. The third sale occurred on Sept. 18 at roughly $220 per share, netting roughly $300 million.

Prearranged trading plans are used by executives to buy or sell shares of their firm on specific dates or target prices. It's a mechanism to wall off company employees from insider trading accusations as long as they stick to the automatic plan.

The SEC first instituted the practice in 2000 and modified it in 2022 to include a 90-day waiting period for starting trades. In some cases, the plans were abused by executives in instances like executing share sales just before an earnings report.

In Stevens's case, he didn't have such a trading plan, but that's not necessarily a red flag on its own. Insiders cashing out of their stock will do so for a variety of reasons that aren't always tied to a company's performance, such as quickly raising liquidity. In Nvidia's case, the move could pour water on the enthusiasm of retail investors to buy into an AI titan that has also attracted short sellers .

The first two stock sales in late August and early September followed a robust Q2 earnings report that caused Nvidia shares to jump about 10% in valuein the following week. Stevens still holds about 27.5 million shares in Nvidia, a colossal position.

articles.title: Zetwerk Q2 loss widens 43% to Rs 88 cr
articles.summary: Zetwerk Q2 loss widens 43% YoY to Rs 88 crore on higher ESOP and finance costs; income rises 18% to Rs 4,653 crore, order book hits Rs 14,595 crore.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Newly listed Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses’ losses widened 43% year-on-year to Rs 88 crore in the September quarter, from Rs 61.6 crore a year earlier, due to higher employee stock-option expenses and finance costs.Total income grew 18% to Rs 4,652.7 crore from Rs 3,936.5 crore. These were its first quarterly results since listing on Oct 23.Employee stock-option charges rose nearly fivefold to Rs 64.4 crore from Rs 13 crore. Zetwerk attributed the increase to one-off vesting linked to its IPO.Losses from continuing operations more than doubled to Rs 53.8 crore from Rs 20.6 crore a year earlier. The remaining Rs 34.3 crore loss came from its discontinued civil infrastructure business, which it plans to sell.The overall loss narrowed from Rs 733 crore in the June quarter. That quarter included a Rs 639 crore provision covering doubtful dues, other assets and expected project losses in the infrastructure business.Zetwerk’s manufacturing order book rose 67% year on year to a record Rs 14,595 crore. It won orders worth Rs 4,613 crore during the September quarter, up 44%. The company said the order book typically converts into revenue over about two years.“Our manufacturing order book is at an all-time high of Rs 14,595 cr, and repeat customers contributed 83% of first-half revenue,” said cofounder and CEO Amrit Acharya.Manufacturing revenue rose 15% to Rs 2,546 crore in the quarter. Its own factories accounted for 60% of manufacturing revenue in the first half, up from 36% a year earlier. International customers contributed 41% of first-half manufacturing revenue, against 36% last year. The company said a greater share of in-house production, international customers and higher-margin products helped improve margins.Zetwerk supplies industrial and consumer products through its own factories and outside suppliers. Its network includes 26 owned facilities across India, the US, Spain and Germany.The company expects finance costs to decline after debt repayment using IPO proceeds, with the full benefit visible from the March quarter. articles.title: Huang's China affair may fix Howard Lutnick, the man who wanted to fix India
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: For commerce secretary Howard Lutnick, the roadmap for major trade deals was simple: countries like India and Brazil
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: For commerce secretary Howard Lutnick, the roadmap for major trade deals was simple: countries like India and Brazil had to be “fixed” to set an example to the world; specifically, PM Modi needed to make a placatory phone call to President Trump; and China needed to be kept dependent on the United States. Except, when it came to selling American AI chips to Beijing, it turns out he was less a hawk and more a dove, like Nvidia's Jensen Huang.Allegations from Lutnick’s own cabinet colleagues that the US commerce department sat on recommendations from other US agencies to sanction China-linked Megaspeed, now accused of spiriting advanced Nvidia AI chips to Beijing via a honeytrap operation, has suddenly put the commerce secretary’s job on the line. In a stunning development on Thursday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly threw Lutnick under the bus, disclosing that the Departments of Treasury, War, USTR, and State were all in favor of putting Megaspeed on the “entity list” for months, “but commerce has the pen.”"You will have to ask commerce about their internal process...I am frustrated when President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s….any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies and gives the Chinese an advantage," Bessent told reporters in more public dissonance in the Trump cabinet.Despite occasionally presenting himself as a China hawk, Lutnick's philosophy when it comes to AI chips was hardly a secret and he had articulated it with characteristic bluntness over months: America, he argued, should sell enough advanced chips to Chinese developers to get them "addicted to the American technology stack." The idea, which was also advanced by Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, was to keep the US ahead technologically while ensuring that China continued to use American chips, software, and infrastructure rather than letting it build an entirely independent ecosystem that could eventually challenge US primacy.The problem with Bessent’s dumping on Lutnick though is that President Trump himself previously approved sales of certain Nvidia processors, including H200 chips, to China, broadly reflecting Huang's and Lutnick's argument that America should compete commercially rather than surrender the Chinese market altogether. At the same time, Trump also reportedly authorised crackdowns on suspected chip diversion on three occasions this year, only for implementation to stall, reflecting the conflict between backing the commercial logic of selling chips and the national-security imperative of preventing their diversion.Trump, for his part, has not yet abandoned Lutnick amid growing bipartisan Congressional scrutiny. The White House has declared that the President maintains "complete confidence" in Lutnick, praising his contribution to America First trade policies, tariffs and manufacturing investments. But the President's own position on China chips is hardly consistent with the tough line being demanded by national-security officials.Beyond the strategic dimension of Washington trying to maintain the technological upper hand, the issue is becoming a political hot potato domestically with Democratic lawmakers, chuffed by the mid-term election verdict, jumping on the issue. Republican Senators are also emboldened by results that have weakened Trump. “This whole thing is an intergalactic freak show….how do they know the chips went to the company (Megapseed) and not to the Communist Party of China?’ asked Louisiana Republican John Kennedy.More fireworks and disclosures are expected ahead of Congressional hearings in the coming weeks. The Republican chairs of three House panels -- Foreign Affairs, the Select Committee on China, and Intelligence -- have asked Jensen Huang to sit for a joint, closed-door interview on December 1, followed by a public hearing before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3. Lutnick is also scheduled to appear before the Senate Banking Committee on December 10.The latest developments have dramatically raised the stakes for both Lutnick and Huang amid growing infamy for the Nvidia founder and CEO. Reports of Huang having a third extramarital relationship involving another Nvidia employee emerged on Thursday, even as the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday that Huang had privately belittled his successor Colette Kress, describing her as "a deer in the headlights" during a meeting this summer, after she questioned some of his increasingly aggressive investment decisions.Trump, meanwhile, has remained remarkably sympathetic to Huang, even after his departure from Nvidia. In a pre-recorded interview with Stephen Smith aired on Thurday, the President said he had spoken to the embattled icon on Wednesday and that "he's going through hell," while describing him as a "tremendous talent" who would somehow land on his feet.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: SpaceX faces key launch test tonight with 'double catch' of Starship and Super Heavy Booster
articles.summary: SpaceX faces a key launch test with Starship's latest mission coming up Friday night. The test comes as SpaceX stock traded in a state of flux this week.
articles.body:
SpaceX ( SPCX ) faces a key launch test with Starship's latest mission scheduled for Friday night at 5:45 ET. The test comes as SpaceX stock traded in a state of flux this week.

SpaceX says the upcoming test — Flight 15 — will attempt a "double catch" of both the Super Heavy Booster and Starship upper stage for the first time at its launch site in Boca Chica, Texas. "If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," the company said.

In addition to the catch, the Starship upper stage's primary objectives include deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites. SpaceX says the V3 satellites will "greatly expand the network's capacity and user speeds," with each Starlink V3 satellite adding 1 Terabit of capacity to the constellation, with all 26 satellites equaling around 10 separate Starlink V2 Mini launches on the smaller Falcon 9 rocket.

A successful test and continued success for Starship is of critical importance for SpaceX. The company will soon phase out its workhorse Falcon 9 rocket for Starship and its Heavy Booster, which will allow more payload per launch and will ultimately be cheaper to use per ton of cargo sent to space.

Plus, Starship and its larger payload will be critical for SpaceX's desire to launch and deploy an orbital data center constellation.

Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas called Starship Flight 15 "one of the most significant catalysts in SpaceX's 20+ year history," and the flight gives investors the "opportunity" to revisit SpaceX from an investment standpoint ahead of the launch.

The launch comes to cap off an interesting week for the stock. Though it is up 2% for the week, it has surged and slipped throughout the week — at one point hitting highs of $148.44 and $135.40.

In addition, CEO Elon Musk's goal of combining his two biggest companies - SpaceX and Tesla ( TSLA ) - is humming along.

Bloomberg reported on Thursday that the companies could announce a merger as early as December, reflecting Musk's desire to move quickly while the boards and advisors hammer out the deal terms and structure. However, there's talk the deal announcement could slip into early 2027.

Timing is everything, as post-midterms there will be plenty of scrutiny of Musk and his companies via Congressional hearings. The companies would also most likely hope to close any transaction while a M&A friendly Trump White House is still in power.

articles.title: Nvidia co-founder Chris Malachowsky is seen as a potential successor to Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia co-founder Chris Malachowsky is one of many individuals who could take over the company as CEO.
articles.body:
With Jensen Huang out as Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO following his affair scandals, CFO Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO.

The company's board is now searching both internally and externally for a permanent replacement for Huang.

Rene Haas, the CEO of Arm Holdings, is a contender , and Ian Buck, Nvidia's head of hyperscale and high-performance computing, is considered an early frontrunner for the position thanks to his strong technical expertise.

Buck created the CUDA software that enables developers to use Nvidia's chips for general-purpose computing, helping turn the company into the AI juggernaut it is today.

Nvidia co-founder Chris Malachowsky could also step in to serve as CEO.

An accomplished engineer with nearly 40 patents to his name, Malachowsky is an Nvidia fellow and senior technology executive, a biography on the company's site states.

Malachowsky has overseen efforts within Nvidia, including its operations and engineering. He's also led its research organization.

But whether Malachowsky, or anyone, for that matter, can fully replace Huang remains to be seen. The former CEO was Nvidia's biggest champion and the face of the AI era.

He hosted enormous keynote events, clad in his signature leather jackets, and traveled the world, drawing massive crowds as an AI ambassador.

He also had the kind of deep connections necessary to attract customers and make investments in a variety of AI-related businesses.

For now, Kress will serve as a steadying force within Nvidia as it seeks to find its footing following the past week's drama.

But the company's board will have to make a decision sooner or later, and whoever it chooses will determine the future of one of the world's most important companies. Sounds easy.

articles.title: ‘Deer in the headlights’: Colette Kress went from clashing with Huang to leading Nvidia
articles.summary: Nvidia former-CEO Jensen Huang has reported to have previously confronted the new acting CEO and CFO Colette Kress, likening her to “a deer in the
articles.body: Nvidia former-CEO Jensen Huang has reported to have previously confronted the new acting CEO and CFO Colette Kress, likening her to “a deer in the headlights”.Huang interrupted Kress during her presentation, according to a person familiar with his remarks cited by The Wall Street Journal. He later called her a “reporting CFO”, suggesting she could report the numbers but was not equipped to help him shape strategy or make decisions.The exchange offered a glimpse into the tensions inside Nvidia as Huang pushed the company deeper into an increasingly risky web of financing arrangements. Kress had been questioning the scale of those commitments, including deals involving companies that were also major buyers of Nvidia chips.Now, following Huang’s departure on Thursday, Kress has been named Nvidia’s interim chief executive, putting her in charge of a company grappling with questions over its AI investments, internal oversight and succession planning.According to Reuters, Kress and her team had clashed with Huang and the company's sales executives over multibillion-dollar financing deals involving OpenAI and AI infrastructure firms such as Lambda. The arrangements were part of Huang's effort to support customers and sustain demand for Nvidia chips, but critics warned that the company risked financing its own customers and creating a circular AI economy.One of the biggest proposals involved an Ohio data-centre project for OpenAI. Nvidia had considered providing a $250-billion financial backstop to help the AI company secure loans for the facility, which was expected to be filled with Nvidia chips. Kress subsequently reworked the proposal, cutting Nvidia's initial commitment to $120 billion, people familiar with the deal told Reuters.The Wall Street Journal reported that Kress had raised questions about how Nvidia should select such deals, value the guarantees and calculate their returns. She also tried to rein in Huang's son-in-law, Nico Caprez, who had been helping arrange financing for cloud providers and data-centre developers.Nvidia eventually paused some of its financing initiatives, with proposals facing closer scrutiny from the executive team and board. Huang also pushed his staff to develop a framework for assessing whether guarantees were worthwhile, including the chip sales they could generate.Kress had publicly defended the strategy even as concerns mounted. In August, she rejected the description of Nvidia's arrangements as circular financing, arguing that they would deliver strong returns.“We recognise the scale of this support, and we know some will call this circular financing. We see it differently,” she said. “The equity returns on our invested capital will be excellent.”Her appointment now places her at the centre of the challenge she had once questioned. Reuters described Kress as a pragmatist who could reassure customers and suppliers during the transition, and potentially adopt a less confrontational approach to Washington than Huang, particularly on export controls.But whether she can preserve the technological ambition and appetite for risk that powered Nvidia's rise remains an open question. Some analysts have questioned whether a finance executive can provide the kind of technology-driven leadership the company needs.Kress joined Nvidia in 2013 after finance roles at Microsoft, Cisco and Texas Instruments. She has spent more than a decade as Huang's CFO, watching the company's valuation soar as its chips became indispensable to the AI industry.In a memo to employees on Thursday, she praised Huang and said she would continue “building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years”.Her appointment comes as Nvidia faces a leadership crisis triggered by revelations about Huang's personal relationships. He stepped down after reports of two extramarital affairs, one involving a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence operative and another involving an Nvidia employee, according to Reuters.Kress must now take charge of the company as it confronts not only uncertainty over its future leadership and investment strategy, but also the fallout from the circumstances surrounding Huang's exit.Money habits form by age 7. articles.body:
( NewsNation ) – The U.S. Postal Service announced it will raise domestic shipping prices, making the fuel surcharge permanent in 2027.

USPS said that it will make a temporary 8 percent surcharge, which was first implemented in April of this year, permanent, with an additional 3 percent “given the recent further elevation of fuel prices.”

The surcharge will reportedly be reevaluated in July 2027 based on fuel prices in the first half of 2027.

The Postal Service also filed a notice to increase prices for USPS Ground Advantage, Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express and Parcel Select. The change would raise domestic shipping service prices by 5.9 percent on average, according to a news release.

USPS added that it is also changing international mail and shipping rates, raising prices by an average of 7.9 percent for some services.

“The USPS governors believe these new rates will keep the Postal Service competitive while providing the agency with much needed revenue as it continues to struggle with financial issues,” the agency said in a statement.

articles.title: US Supreme Court to consider lawsuit over Robinhood's 2021 IPO
articles.summary: Nov 13 (Reuters) - The US Supreme Court agreed on Friday to consider an effort by Robinhood Markets to shut down a lawsuit accusing the online brokerage of m...
articles.body:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - The US Supreme Court agreed on Friday to consider an effort by Robinhood Markets to shut down a lawsuit accusing the online brokerage of misleading investors ‌about its financials and growth prospects for its initial public offering.

Robinhood appealed a lower court's decision ‌to revive the proposed class action by plaintiffs who alleged that it failed to adequately disclose the negative impact of a meme stock ​and cryptocurrency frenzy that dried up before it went public in July 2021 and other changes in its performance prior to the IPO.

The Supreme Court is expected to hear arguments in the case and issue a ruling by the end of June.

President Donald Trump's administration had urged the Supreme Court to hear the appeal, and backed Robinhood's ‌position.

Investors who acquired Robinhood shares tied to ⁠the IPO sued under provisions of the Securities Act of 1933, a federal investor protection law that seeks to ensure companies disclose accurate information needed to make informed investment ⁠decisions.

Results following the IPO that showed declines in revenue and key performance indicators caused the Menlo Park, California-based company's stock price to drop sharply, the plaintiffs said.

They claimed that Robinhood made misleading statements and omissions in IPO documents by not ​disclosing a ​shift in revenue to fad trading in social media-driven ​meme stocks like GameStop and cryptocurrency dogecoin, which ‌subsided prior to the IPO, as well as an "exodus of its traditional customers." Those alleged omissions threatened Robinhood's financial prospects, the plaintiffs alleged.

Robinhood rejected the claims, contending that because of the trading volume spikes at the beginning of 2021, its IPO documents made extensive disclosures about future risks and warned about a downturn from the meme-stock and dogecoin-driven peaks.

The lead plaintiffs in the lawsuit, first filed in 2021, are Vinod Sodha, a psychiatrist from ‌Beverly Hills, California, and his daughter Amee Sodha, a physician ​from Millburn, New Jersey.

US District Judge Edward Chen in San Francisco ​dismissed the lawsuit in 2024 after finding that ​the plaintiffs' claims of Robinhood's failings were insufficient for the case to proceed.

The San ‌Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals revived ​the challenge in 2025, finding ​that Chen applied the wrong standards under the securities laws and regulations at issue in the case.

Robinhood urged the Supreme Court to hear the case, saying that the 9th Circuit's decision exposes companies ​to massive liability while imposing burdensome disclosure ‌requirements that risk burying investors in trivial information.

The case "concerns classic half-truths in the registration statement ​that Robinhood used for its IPO in July 2021," the plaintiffs told the Supreme Court.

(Reporting by ​Andrew Chung in New York; Editing by Will Dunham)

articles.title: Microsoft's latest outage hit Outlook and Copilot — what it means for your email
articles.summary: No one has confirmed what caused the Microsoft outage that took down Outlook and Copilot, and nothing links it to layoffs or AI, but it's not the first time...
articles.body:
Millions of office workers got an unplanned break from email Thursday. Their bosses' favorite new AI tool got one too.

A Microsoft ( MSFT ) outage that began midday Thursday knocked out Outlook and other workplace apps worldwide, with Downdetector logging reports from 74 countries within about an hour. By Friday, Microsoft said it was seeing "encouraging recovery progress."

The damage reached Microsoft's AI. Copilot couldn't access users' email, files, or calendars, and the Microsoft connectors for OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) Claude broke too.

Microsoft says more than 430 million people use its Microsoft 365 apps.

Your email isn't lost. Microsoft stretched its email timeout to 48 hours , so messages sent to you keep trying to deliver instead of bouncing back.

There isn't much to fix on your end. Resetting your password or reinstalling Outlook won't help, though desktop Outlook may still show mail it already downloaded.

If your company pays for Microsoft 365, it may be owed money. Microsoft promises 99.9% uptime , about 43 minutes of downtime a month, with credits of 25% to 100% of the monthly fee when it falls short. Your IT department has to file the claim.

Microsoft is hard to replace, which is usually good news for its shareholders. Pershing Square CEO Bill Ackman, whose fund owns Microsoft stock, said at Yahoo Finance Invest on Thursday that Microsoft is "the gateway to how people interact with the basic workflows of a desk worker," which makes it "a much more difficult position to dislodge."

This week showed the other side of that.

Microsoft has blamed its own changes or maintenance for Microsoft 365 disruptions in at least six months this year, from a nearly 10-hour outage in January to a spam-filter update that bounced real email earlier this month.

Australia's home affairs minister, Tony Burke, said Microsoft believes it's dealing with "an update that has gone awry," much like the 2024 CrowdStrike meltdown.

Have you tried turning it off and on again?

Microsoft reached for the oldest fix in the help desk manual, saying Thursday it was "restarting affected servers to return them to service."

It didn't stick. Servers that came back went down again once traffic returned, and on Friday Microsoft was reversing a recent network change without confirming it was the cause.

The outage comes as Microsoft trims its workforce while spending heavily on AI. It offered buyouts to about 60,000 employees in October, and those who accept leave Dec. 31. CEO Satya Nadella said last year that AI writes "maybe 20%, 30%" of Microsoft's code .

articles.title: 'Nothing has changed': Why some Nvidia stock bulls aren't wavering after Jensen Huang ouster
articles.summary: The bulls refuse to completely throw in the towel on Nvidia.
articles.body:
Wall Street hasn't totally given up on Nvidia's ( NVDA ) stock. While there has been a steady stream of price targets this week and a few downgrades, a lot of analysts who cover the company are staying bullish.

Their argument is captured in one note from Wedbush analyst Matthew Bryson.

"Nothing has changed," Bryson wrote on Friday ahead of Nvidia's earnings next week. "We again expect NVDA to exceed its forecast and to guide FQ4 above Street."

"Management has tended to leave a fair bit [of] wiggle room in guidance, allowing for meaningful upside when reporting numbers and we expect NVDA will deliver another beat and raise quarter."

"A strong hyperscaler spending backdrop augmented by increased spending at neoclouds and model builders (in particular xAI) is persisting into the out quarters as highlighted by results and guidance from Taiwan Semiconductor, AMD, SuperMicro, Foxconn, etc. as well as our own supply chain checks."

"We believe NVDA has built a best in industry position with material and component suppliers through at least next year at a point where component and material access, not end demand, is defining shipments."

It has been a brutal week for the once-untouchable Nvidia founder Jensen Huang.

Huang was ousted as CEO of the company he founded in 1993 amid a shocking turn of events.

According to the New York Times , Huang, whose relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy has embroiled the company in scandal this week, also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, one of Huang's 60 or so direct reports.

Reuters reported late Thursday that Huang had a relationship with another Nvidia employee. The employee's name was not released. Huang has been married to his wife Lori for more than 40 years.

Nvidia CEO Huang resigns amid affair scandals

Who is Colette Kress, Nvidia's new interim CEO?

3 challenges for a post-Jensen Huang Nvidia

While Nvidia looks for a successor, the board has installed longtime CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO.

Interestingly, Nvidia's stock is only down 12% for the week. We say only because, at one point, not seeing Huang atop Nvidia would have been unthinkable, and given the leadership uncertainty, one would think the stock would be down a lot more.

"Questions about data center financing, politics, and most significantly, former CEO Jensen Huang's sudden resignation have seemingly sucked up the oxygen that had been fueling NVDA's momentum since the release of ChatGPT4.0," Bryson said.

Some oxygen is still being pumped into Nvidia's stock, it appears.

articles.title: 'Extraordinary circumstances': US grounds all departing flights over safety concerns
articles.summary: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) on Friday ordered a nationwide ground stop, citing “extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety”,
articles.body: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) on Friday ordered a nationwide ground stop, citing “extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety”, after a communications outage affected air traffic control operations across the country.The FAA directed all departing flights to remain grounded until further notice, while inbound international flights would be handled on a case-by-case basis. The agency also warned that equipment outages could lead to airborne holding at airports across the national airspace system.The FAA had earlier announced a ground stop at Chicago O'Hare International Airport due to a communications issue, according to its website.US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the communications problem had affected all 22 regional air traffic control centres responsible for directing aircraft travelling between airports nationwide. FAA technicians were investigating the issue.US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication that the outage was the result of a deliberate attack.“There is no indication yet that "this was a nefarious attack against us. It's just a telecommunications outage,” Mullin said.“Everybody's safe. There's no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they're flying,” he added.Authorities have not provided a timeline for resuming normal flight operations. Mullin said investigators would also examine whether the outage was linked to the FAA's nationwide rollout of a new artificial intelligence system designed to identify problems and recommend alternative flight routes. However, the system operates from a single location near Washington, DC, and sends recommendations to air traffic control centres.The nationwide ground stop was the first since January 2023, when a malfunction in a key FAA computer system disrupted flight operations. Before that, a similar nationwide restriction had been imposed following the September 11, 2001, attacks.The disruption has also drawn attention to the ageing technology used by the country's air traffic control system. The government has been working to modernise the infrastructure since Congress approved $12.5 billion for the project last year. The overhaul includes replacing miles of ageing copper wires with fibre-optic lines and gradually upgrading radio systems at airports across the country.However, significant work remains. Duffy has said an additional $30 billion would be required to complete the modernisation, with the White House lobbying Congress to approve the funding.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Family Dollar to pay $63 million to settle allegations that it routinely overcharged customers
articles.summary: Family Dollar will pay $63 million to settle state and federal allegations that it routinely charged customers more at the register than the prices displayed...
articles.body:
Family Dollar will pay $63 million to settle state and federal allegations that it routinely charged customers more at the register than the prices displayed on its shelves, website and mobile app.

The Federal Trade Commission and 17 states filed federal charges against the company Thursday and announced the proposed settlement the same day. The settlement must still be approved by a judge.

According to the FTC's complaint, consumers from across the country have been reporting price discrepancies at Family Dollar for years. In January 2025, for example, consumers from at least seven states reported that Family Dollar refused to honor a "2 for $20" sale on a package of diapers, even though the price was advertised on its mobile app and on shelf tags.

One Michigan consumer took a picture of the "2 for $20" shelf tag and brought it to the register, but reported that the store manager said the price was wrong and quickly removed the shelf tag, the complaint said.

Over the last five years, state and local regulators have cited Family Dollar for thousands of pricing violations, resulting in fines of more than $3 million, the complaint said. It has also entered into multiple settlements with state attorneys general and consumer protection agencies over inaccurate pricing.

Family Dollar said Friday it will work with the FTC and state agencies to meet the settlement's requirements and provide clear information to customers about how the settlement could impact them.

"We take our responsibility to deliver a positive shopping experience seriously," Family Dollar spokeswoman Janella Escobar said in a statement. "We remain focused on strengthening pricing accuracy across our stores and maintaining our customers' trust."

Family Dollar, which is privately owned and based in Chesapeake, Virginia, has more than 8,000 U.S. discount stores. It reported revenue of $13 billion in its most recent fiscal year, according to a company statement.

The case is similar to one the FTC and 20 states filed last month against Dollar General, a rival bargain chain. That case is ongoing.

Under the proposed settlement, Family Dollar will be required to establish a $40 million consumer redress fund payable to eligible consumers. The company must notify customers about the fund through notices in stores and on its digital platforms.

The settlement requires Family Dollar to establish a $20 million discount program for its customers and pay $3 million to the states involved in the case. Those states are: Alabama, Arkansas, Colorado, Florida, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Nebraska, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Utah and Wisconsin.

The settlement also requires Family Dollar to implement a pricing accuracy program that is independently assessed and annually certified.

Airline stocks fell right before Friday's close after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop. Departing flights cannot take off, while flights already in the air may continue to their destination.

Transportation Department Secretary Sean Duffy said in a statement that there is a "communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers."

Around 5 p.m. Eastern, the FAA said in a statement on X that the action was taken out of caution.

"There has been a temporary telecommunications outage — out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted. Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis."

Shares of American Airlines ( AAL ), Southwest ( LUV ), JetBlue ( JBLU ), Delta Air Lines ( DAL ), and United Airlines ( UAL ) all moved lower on the news.

This is extremely rare. The last time that the FAA halted all US departures was in January of 2023 due to a system outage. Prior to that, traffic was halted after the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

Microsoft said in a statement posted on X that its outage is not related to this incident.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A global Microsoft 365 outage disrupted operations across offices as Outlook email, Teams calendars and the tools that connect ChatGPT and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A global Microsoft 365 outage disrupted operations across offices as Outlook email, Teams calendars and the tools that connect ChatGPT and Claude to Microsoft's workplace services remained paralysed.The problem, which started late Thursday (India time), was partially restored on Friday evening though intermittent issues persisted. By late evening in India, Microsoft said mailbox access was improving, and delayed emails were being processed, while stating that it had found no indication of a cyberattack. This was the second disruption since Oct 2025 when MS Azure services faced an eight-hour-long global outage.Companies that rely on MS services were forced to opt for other alternatives such as Slack, Webex and Zoom to keep their operations going. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles cited the outage in a stock exchange filing and shifted its quarterly results webcast with Jaguar Land Rover executives to StreamCart. IBM reportedly moved workplace communication to Slack during the disruption. HDFC Bank told customers on X that its banking services remained available.Airlines and airport operators said operations continued while email communication with passengers was disrupted. Travellers who bought or changed tickets during the outage had to download them from the airline's website or app if their confirmation email did not arrive. Airport operators said they were unable to send emails. Air India rerouted incoming messages, IndiGo directed passengers needing urgent help to its 6E Skai chatbot, and Akasa Air asked customers to call or use social media.Overseas, Australia's sanctions office directed urgent enquiries to the phone. In UK, National Pharmacy Association warned that disruption to NHS email could delay prescriptions. On Thursday, Microsoft first flagged trouble accessing work mailboxes in the Americas. In India, complaints picked up mainly as offices opened on Friday.Microsoft starts reversing recent network changeOutage tracker Downdetector logged around 3,800 Outlook complaints at 10.12am, close to the overnight peak.“We regret the disruption today’s outage has caused for many of our customers,” Puneet Chandok, president of Microsoft India and South Asia, wrote on LinkedIn. “Our global teams continue to work with urgency to resolve the issue.”The problem centred on Exchange Online, the service that runs workplace email and calendars. Some servers unexpectedly went offline, leaving fewer machines to handle the same workload. Some stopped responding again when users reconnected.Microsoft began reversing a recent network change that coincided with the start of the disruption and was investigating whether it triggered the outage. Teams chats and calls could still work even when calendars and meeting invites failed.Anthropic said most email, calendar and search requests through Claude’s Microsoft 365 connector were failing. Some users could not open Claude for Outlook, while others had trouble performing mail and calendar tasks. OpenAI said ChatGPT users could have trouble setting up new connections to Microsoft services and that some existing connections were also failing.Anthropic separately investigated sign-in errors affecting Claude.ai, Claude Code and its developer platform. articles.title: Khambata 'strategised' to oust Srinivasan, say Tata Trusts VCs
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Two senior Tata Trusts trustees have accused a former colleague of helping the present leadership of the Trusts to reinforce control at the
articles.body: MUMBAI: Two senior Tata Trusts trustees have accused a former colleague of helping the present leadership of the Trusts to reinforce control at the expense of his own fiduciary duties and the sanctity of the Tata model of governance.In a letter dated Nov 11, vice-chairmen of the Trusts, Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh, said Darius Khambata's account of the dispute between Noel Tata and a section of trustees was "incomplete in several material respects."They alleged that Khambata "strategised" to temporarily oust Srinivasan as a Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) trustee so that two new trustees could be inducted in Nov 2025. "There was nothing consensual about that process," they wrote.Their reply targets Khambata's Nov 2 letter, which described a Tata Sons listing as "existential" for the Trusts and said the company's engagement with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had been neither meaningful nor successful. Srinivasan and Singh said the record showed otherwise.Tata Sons began talking to the RBI in 2023, repaid its debt and applied for deregistration in March 2024, they said. The engagement continued after that. "The trustees were kept informed throughout, and neither you nor any other trustee described the effort as inadequate at the time," they wrote.The RBI ruled after a two-year review that Tata Sons remained a systemically significant institution bound by the listing framework. The outcome, they said, reflected the regulator's judgment and "cannot be attributed to any deficiency in advocacy." "If, by 'meaningful' advocacy, you mean advocacy that secures preferential treatment or circumvents the applicable rules, then that would not be consistent with the Tata model you seek to uphold."The letter rejected Khambata's claim that listing would threaten the Tata model. "We have seen no evidence for that proposition," the vice-chairmen said. They pointed to Novo Nordisk, Hershey, Lundbeck and Demant - each listed, each controlled or anchored by a foundation or trust. "An institution's character is preserved by the quality of its governance and accountability, not by its listing status."Khambata, a senior advocate, did not seek reappointment as a trustee when his term ended on Nov 8.Closer to home, they cited TCS, Tata Steel, Tata Power and Tata Motors, all listed and all of which have made long-gestation investments. "Disclosure and accountability bring discipline to how capital is allocated; they do not limit vision." The Trusts would stay shareholders of Tata Sons after a listing, and their "shareholding, dividends and the philanthropy those dividends fund would be unaffected".They asked whether Khambata's real concern was the Tata model or control of Tata Sons by the Trusts' present leadership. Where control becomes "an end in itself", they said, questions arise about trustees' fiduciary duties and the Trusts' continued entitlement to tax exemption. A listing of Tata Sons would end Trusts' superior voting rights on the company's board, which is why Trusts chairman Noel Tata is opposed to an IPO.The letter said the trustees of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) unanimously recommended Chandrasekaran for a third term as executive chairman on July 28, 2025. Khambata supported that resolution and drafted it, they said. Two new trustees were inducted into SDTT on Nov 11, 2025, materially altering its balance, and Khambata proposed one of them, they said. In Feb 2026 Chandrasekran's reappointment was deferred, and no Trusts resolution reversed the July 28, 2025 decision.Khambata in his Nov 2 letter had called that resolution "overtaken" by events in Aug and Sept 2026. Srinivasan and Singh disagreed. "A unanimous resolution of trustees is not overtaken merely because honouring it later became difficult."They quoted a July 10, 2025 note from Khambata to Chandrasekaran, in which he called the group's results and plans "even more impressive than I'd imagined". Eighteen days later he backed the reappointment. "We would like to know what changed between that letter and the position you now take?" they asked.A trustee who praised the chairman in those terms, they added, and then "stood by passively while his reappointment was left in doubt for seven months, owes the Trusts and the public an explanation".Chandrasekaran concluded that the dignity of his office was being compromised by the delay and decided not to offer himself for reappointment, they said. The nomination and remuneration committee of Tata Sons unanimously asked him to reconsider. The company's board acted on Sept 17, they said, to end an uncertainty it had not created. On Sept 17, the Tata Sons board reappointed Chandrasekaran as chairman for a third term. Srinivasan supported the decision, while Noel opposed it.The Trusts, they said, were "more divided today than at any point in living memory". Khambata had argued, citing the Supreme Court's judgment in Tata Group v Cyrus Mistry, that a Trust nominee director must protect the Trusts' interests and that "there cannot be two classes of trustees". Srinivasan and Singh disputed that reading. "It did not extinguish a director's fiduciary duty to the company," they said, "nor turn a Trust nominee into a delegate bound to vote the Trusts' line."On the Sept 11, 2025 vote not to renew Singh's tenure as a Tata Sons director, they said Khambata's own account showed a board seat decided by the need to secure a voting outcome rather than by the nominee's merit. They called that "difficult to reconcile" with the principles in his Nov 2 letter. "What you describe as betrayal is, in substance, a difference of view."No amount of spin-doctoring could mask what had happened, Srinivasan and Singh said, and that "applies to all concerned".Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Oil supply to overtake demand in Dec quarter: IEA
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Global oil supply is set to exceed demand in the Dec quarter for the first time since the US-Iran war began, with recovering exports from West
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Global oil supply is set to exceed demand in the Dec quarter for the first time since the US-Iran war began, with recovering exports from West Asia easing the supply crunch even as attacks on shipping continue, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday. A surplus supply also augurs well for prices with analysts suggesting that they will cool down, provided there are no fresh flareups in the region.The agency expects global oil supply to average around 105 million barrels per day (mbd) in the Dec quarter, 1.7 mbd higher than demand. This marks a sharp turnaround from its earlier forecast of a supply deficit.The recovery in supplies has eased pressure on crude prices. Brent Dated crude fell 32% from a peak of $136 per barrel in early Oct to around $93 per barrel, although it remained $22 per barrel above pre-war levels, IEA said. On Friday, Brent was trading at $95 a barrel, while the cost for Indian refiners on Thursday was estimated at $91.15.The increase in global oil supplies should have a moderating effect on prices, but replenishment of strategic reserves by countries that drew heavily from them during the conflict could push demand up, said Prashant Vasisht, senior vice-president at ICRA. Damaged oil infrastructure may also take time to recover, while continued geopolitical uncertainty could keep a premium on crude prices, he added."If the situation remains the same, prices may cool down to $75-80 per barrel, but they may not return to pre-war levels of $65-70 per barrel any time soon," he said.The improvement in supplies comes as West Asian producers step up exports despite disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Gulf oil exports, excluding Oman, rose to 18.4 mbd in Oct, recovering to 74% of pre-war levels.Global oil supply rose by 2.3 mbd to 105.4 mbd in Oct, following an increase of 3 mbd in Sept. IEA expects supply to decline by an average 4.8 mbd in 2026 before rebounding by 6.6 mbd in 2027, led by a recovery in Gulf production.Global oil inventories rose by 52 million barrels in Oct, the first increase since June. Much of the build-up was in oil in transit, with volumes on water increasing by 86 million barrels, while on-land inventories continued to decline.On the demand side, IEA expects global oil consumption to decline by 2.7 mbd to 102.3 mbd in 2026 before recovering by 2 mbd in 2027.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Profits of banks rise 20% on interest income, loan growth
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Indian banks' net profit rose 20% year-on-year to Rs 1.2 lakh crore in Q2FY27, driven by higher interest income, loan growth and one-time gains of
articles.body: MUMBAI: Indian banks' net profit rose 20% year-on-year to Rs 1.2 lakh crore in Q2FY27, driven by higher interest income, loan growth and one-time gains of around Rs 10,000 crore at large public sector banks (PSBs). The growth was also aided by a weak base, with profits having risen just 4.2% in Q2FY26.According to a CareEdge Ratings report, net profit of scheduled commercial banks (SCBs) remained above Rs 1 lakh crore for the fourth consecutive quarter. Net interest income (NII) grew 15.4% as bank credit expanded around 19%. However, higher bond yields during the quarter sharply reduced treasury income. Profit growth varied across bank groups. PSBs reported a 15.9% increase in net profit, while private sector banks (PVBs) recorded 25.1% growth. Both groups reported similar operating profit growth, with the difference largely explained by provisions. PSBs' provisions rose 9.2%, while those of private banks fell 25.1%, reflecting an easing of stress in microfinance and unsecured lending at other private banks. The latter's growth was also supported by a weak base as their profits declined 4% in Q2FY26."Core lending drove bank earnings this quarter. Operating profit grew 13-15% y-o-y in both bank groups, so provisions explain the gap in their profit growth. Other private banks are catching up as credit costs ease," said Vineet Jain, senior director at CareEdge Ratings. He said the return on assets gap between other private banks and large private banks had halved over the past year, while higher provisions ahead of the expected credit loss (ECL) rules could weigh on returns.The report, which analysed 30 banks comprising 14 PSBs and 16 private banks, said profit growth was likely to moderate in H2FY27. Treasury income could remain weak, while the one-time gains recorded in Q2 are unlikely to recur. The 10-year govt security yield rose to 7.4% by Oct 19, adding to the pressure on treasury earnings.Provisions could also increase as banks build buffers ahead of the transition to ECL-based provisioning from April 1, 2027.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Nvidia’s week of chaos, explained
articles.summary: In a matter of days, a corporate scandal has toppled the leader of the world’s second-most valuable company, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang; thrust his family into the spotlight; raised huge questions about the future of the AI industry; and landed on Washington’s doorstep.
articles.body: In a matter of days, a corporate scandal has toppled the leader of the world’s second-most valuable company, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang; thrust his family into the spotlight; raised huge questions about the future of the AI industry; and landed on Washington’s doorstep. Huang resigned from Nvidia on Thursday morning in the wake of mounting scrutiny following reports of multiple extramarital relationships, including one with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom US officials had been investigating as a potential national security risk. Nvidia’s board named longtime CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. Investors and Wall Street analysts are likely to have big questions for her when Nvidia reports its third-quarter earnings on Tuesday. In the meantime, Jensen Huang and some key members of the Trump administration are facing questions from lawmakers about the sales and transfer of Nvidia chips to China. Huang has been called to testify in a closed-door congressional hearing on December 1; lawmakers have said they will subpoena him if he doesn’t voluntarily agree to testify. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify next month before the Senate Banking Committee, which has also requested to hear from Huang. Huang’s resignation represents a rapid and stunning fall from grace for one of the most powerful men in tech. Huang had run and largely been synonymous with Nvidia in the 33 years since he cofounded it in a Denny’s restaurant in 1993. His Thursday exit was a marked reversal from just days earlier. On Sunday, the Nvidia board said it would investigate whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, but expressed confidence in his leadership and said it did not believe company secrets or national security had been compromised. The same day, Huang admitted to an extramarital affair, but did not name the other party. But in the subsequent days, growing national security concerns on Capitol Hill — as well as reports that Huang had at least one additional extramarital relationship — appeared to force the board’s hand. It convened Wednesday night to weigh Huang’s future, and he was out the next morning. Nvidia’s stock (NVDA) has taken a beating amid the scandal. As of Friday’s close, Nvidia’s shares had fallen 12.75% since the start of the week, erasing roughly $573 billion in market value. That has wider implications beyond just the company and its investors. Nvidia is one of the largest stocks in the S&P 500 — it comprises about 6% of the total value of the index — meaning its decline has broad implications for many people’s investment and retirement accounts.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's exports and imports set new records in Oct, with the value of goods shipped out of the country jumping 45.2% to $49.5 billion, driven
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's exports and imports set new records in Oct, with the value of goods shipped out of the country jumping 45.2% to $49.5 billion, driven by a surge in oil and electronics exports. With imports rising 16.6% to $89.4 billion, the trade deficit widened to a 12-month high of $40 billion."I told you, the Oct export numbers will surprise you! And our 'outlook' looks strong!" commerce & industry minister Piyush Goyal said after the data was released.Official data showed that petroleum product exports soared 140% to $8.9 billion during Oct, while non-oil imports rose 33.5% to $40.6 billion. Electronics clocked a 63% increase to $6.6 billion, and gems and jewellery were up 40% to $3.2 billion. Engineering goods went up 36% to $12.7 billion."The increase in oil exports is partly due to a price effect and demand for refined products has also seen good growth. We are seeing growth across baskets... If we are able to carry on the trajectory, we can move towards the landmark of $1 trillion (goods and services exports) this year," commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal said.During the first half, goods and services exports were estimated at $479 billion, with Agrawal saying that there is usually an acceleration during the second half. On the import front, crude prices resulted in the value of goods entering India jumping 54% to $22.8 billion, while electronics saw an increase of 50% to $14.2 billion in Oct.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Fed unveils 2027 calendar, confirming October meeting will not include rates vote
articles.summary: The Federal Reserve on Thursday released next year’s schedule for its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), confirming that one meeting will feature discussions on strategy and not a vote on interest rates. The Fed said in a release the FOMC will meet eight times in 2027, with the first meeting in late January and subsequent…
articles.body:
The Federal Reserve on Thursday released next year’s schedule for its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), confirming that one meeting will feature discussions on strategy and not a vote on interest rates.

The Fed said in a release the FOMC will meet eight times in 2027, with the first meeting in late January and subsequent meetings at six-week intervals.

On the second and final day of those meetings, the panel will vote on the federal funds rate, with the exception of its gathering Oct. 26-27 next year.

That meeting, the Fed said, will be “dedicated to the discussion of broad monetary policy strategy issues.”

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh announced the change last month, after FOMC officials held interest rates steady at a range of 3.75 percent to 4 percent . The central bank chair said the committee is making the switch for “straightforward” reasons.

“Getting policy right involves assessing near-term developments at timely, regular and information-rich intervals,” he told reporters .

“But it’s equally important we reserve time and space, as an intellectually diverse group, for strategic deliberations — for thinking anew about big questions, looking out over longer time horizons, focusing, as I say, on the left side of the decimal point,” Warsh added.

Warsh raised a change to the FOMC’s schedule during the panel’s July meeting, according to the minutes .

The first-year chair “observed that six scheduled meetings” each year, held every two months, would “allow more information to accumulate between meetings” than under the status quo, the minutes noted .

Warsh said last month he expects the FOMC to have two meetings dedicated to strategy discussions and six for setting monetary policy in 2028. Under the Federal Reserve Act , the panel must meet at least four times per year.

Jason Furman, the chair of the Council of Economic Advisers under former President Obama, praised Warsh’s tweak to the Fed calendar as a “great move” last month.

“I have long thought the Fed spends too much time on the immediate and not nearly enough time thinking about longer-term strategy,” Furman wrote on social platform X .

The change marks the latest example of Warsh, who succeeded former Fed Chair Jerome Powell in May, putting his imprint on the central bank .

The FOMC’s policy statements have skewed away from including “forward guidance,” information about the likely future conduct of monetary policy.

Warsh has also been alone among 19 committee officials in not providing a “dot” prediction about future rate decisions for either of the FOMC’s two quarterly economic projections since he took over .

The Fed chair has laid out his preference for limiting future projections throughout his nearly six months in charge, saying in July market participants “are learning to play the ball, not the referee” without them.

“I understand the desire for rolling forecasts and commentary from this committee. But for our part, we need to observe market reaction to developments, direct and unfiltered,” Warsh told reporters at the time .

articles.body:
Wholesale inflation hit nearly four-year high: BLS

Wholesale annual inflation hit a nearly four-year high in October, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported Friday.

The producer price index (PPI) rose 0.3 percent from September to last month and was up 6.5 percent relative to October 2025. That marked the highest annual increase since producer prices were up 7.4 percent year-over-year in November 2022, the BLS reported.

In September, producer prices were up 6.3 percent on an annual basis, per the PPI. The annual index has risen in each of the last three months , after declining from 5.9 percent in May, to 5.6 percent in June and 4.9 percent in July, per the BLS.

Heather Long, the chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, called the latest PPI data “worrying” on Friday.

“PPI (basically business inflation) is +6.5% in the past year,” Long wrote on social platform X . “That’s even hotter than the ~4% consumer inflation. Businesses are almost certainly going to pass some of those higher costs onto consumers.

“It’s yet another worrisome inflation risk heading into 2027.”

Excluding more volatile food, energy and trade services, the PPI increased by 0.5 percent from September to October, unchanged from its monthly rise from August to September.

Annually, PPI inflation excluding food, energy and trade services prices was 4.9 percent , the BLS noted.

Gas and diesel prices have spiked amid the Iran war , although Long noted the recent rise in producer prices is “not all” due to rising energy prices.

The BLS reported consumer price index (CPI) data for October earlier this week, although last year’s record-long government shutdown limited its ability to collect statistics during October 2025.

The CPI increased by 0.4 percent from September to October, after rising by 0.6 percent from August to September. Annual CPI inflation was 3.7 percent in September , the BLS reported.
